newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan watchdog files complaints against Nomura.
newsitem.headline: Japan watchdog files complaints against Nomura.

text.p: Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), has filed complaints with prosecutors against Nomura Securities Co Ltd and three former Nomura executives, government sources said on Tuesday.

The complaints were filed following the SESC's probe into allegations that the nation's biggest brokerage made illegal compensation payments of 49.7 million yen ($417,000) to a corporate client who has been linked to a "sokaiya" racketeer, the sources said.

Filing a complaint with prosecutors is the first step towards bringing legal action against a company or an individual. The SESC raided Nomura's offices in March in a widening probe into the brokerage's role in the payments.
Sokaiya typically try to extort money from firms by threatening to expose dubious business practices or to disturb shareholders' meetings.

Nomura made a sweeping reshuffle of its top management late last month, hoping to win back public trust in the scandal-tainted brokerage. It has claimed that the company itself was not involved in the payoff scandal.
